summary: A well-built Pre-IELTS listening test: the four parts follow the real IELTS pattern, the scripts are a realistic length, and Parts 1-3 are full of fair distractors (a speaker changes their mind, the wrong option is mentioned first). It is a little gentler than the real test because Part 4's notes repeat the lecturer's sentences almost word for word. The Part 2 matching box also repeated the script word for word, which made it far too easy; that box has now been reworded.
strengths: Part 1 has a correction or distractor on most gaps: German then Italian, the 16th then the 18th, hotel then airport, cash then bank transfer, flight time 8 then meeting time 9.30.
Part 2 MCQs (Q11-14) each mention two wrong options before or after the right one (outgrown the rooms / town hall not sold; age of documents / speed; desk / locker; roof / photograph rumour).
Part 3 is a natural student discussion with real distractors on every MCQ (tutor's advice, voices, technology) and two well-made multi-select sets with mentioned-but-rejected options.
Script lengths (731 / 869 / 867 / 863 words) match real IELTS timing; answers come in question order.
Gap answers are spelled correctly, are heard exactly, and keep to the word limits.

issues.problem: Q15-20 matching box: every correct option repeated the script word for word ('is the busiest part of the archive', 'can only be visited by appointment', 'will move to a different room soon', 'can be searched on screens in the building', 'oldest item in the archive', 'catalogued by volunteers'), so the six questions tested word-spotting, not listening.
issues.change: Reworded the box options as paraphrases with the same letters and keys: B 'attracts more visitors than any other area', C 'requires visitors to arrange a visit in advance', E 'is being organised by unpaid helpers', F 'contains the archive's earliest document', G 'is going to be relocated shortly', H 'can be explored on computers on site' (A and D distractors lightly reworded / kept). The box is not read in the audio, so the recording is unaffected.

issues.problem: Explanation said the 1584 plan is 'hanging' in the map room; the script says it is displayed in low light. The paraphrase pair ['oldest treasure', 'oldest item'] was broken: 'oldest treasure' is not in the script.
issues.change: Explain now says 'displayed'; pair replaced with ['the oldest item anywhere in the archive', 'contains the archive's earliest document'].

issues.problem: Explanation said Sabina 'doubts the sound effects at first' and called the room a 'workshop'; in the script it is Bekzod who argues for them again and the room is the weaving room.
issues.change: Rewrote the explanation to match the script; evidence capitalisation matched to the script.

issues.problem: Explanation invented details ('she will email them next week'); the script says she will contact the drama department on Monday. The pair ['find out who is available', 'arrange'] used a word that only appeared in the explanation.
issues.change: Explanation corrected; pair removed (the option repeats the script exactly, so there is no real paraphrase to teach).

issues.problem: Pair ['obstacles', 'wards'] was not a paraphrase: 'wards' is the answer word and 'obstacles' is also in the notes.
issues.change: Replaced with ['strike them and stop', 'blocked the wrong key'].

issues.problem: Pair ['unclaimed', 'went unbeaten']: neither side is in the script or the notes.
issues.change: Replaced with ['put one of his locks', 'displayed a lock'].

issues.problem: Part 4 notes copy the lecture almost word for word ('built almost entirely from', 'levers cut to different depths', 'warned the owner that a wrong key had been tried', 'small flat key ... cut by machine', 'the weakest part of any system is the'), so the lecture part is easier than a real Part 4, where the notes paraphrase the speaker.
issues.change: Suggest rewording the note lines (not the script), e.g. Q31 'made mainly of {{31}}', Q36 'levers of varying {{36}}', Q38 'alerted the {{38}} to an attempt with the wrong key', Q39 'could be mass-produced by {{39}}', Q40 'testers say the least reliable element is the {{40}}'.

issues.problem: The note says a false keyhole 'was often added', but the lecturer gives it as one favourite example, not as a common practice.
issues.change: Suggest 'a false {{35}} could be added to mislead a thief'.

issues.problem: Part 1 has only one spelled-out item (the surname). Real Part 1s usually spell out a second item, such as a street, company or email name.
issues.change: For future sets, add a second spelled item; this one cannot change because the audio is recorded.
